hints: Look carefully at what region D means in the Venn diagram. Which of the three named molecules does it belong to?
Remember that every ester bond in a triglyceride and every peptide bond in a protein contains a C=O double bond. How many of these bonds does each molecule have?
walkthrough:
**Read the Venn diagram**

First, notice what each circle means. The top circle is saturated triglyceride, the bottom left is collagen and the bottom right is haemoglobin.

Region D is right in the centre, so it is a feature shared by all three molecules.

**Check the saturated triglyceride**

A triglyceride is formed by three condensation reactions between glycerol and fatty acids. This creates three ester bonds.

Each ester bond contains one C=O double bond, so one triglyceride has three double bonds. That is already at least two, even though the fatty acid chains are saturated.

**Check the two proteins**

Collagen and haemoglobin are both proteins made of many amino acids joined by peptide bonds. Each peptide bond contains one C=O double bond.

Because both proteins contain hundreds of peptide bonds, they each contain far more than two double bonds. Haemoglobin also has extra double bonds in its four haem groups.

**Pick the shared region**

Since saturated triglyceride, collagen and haemoglobin all contain at least two double bonds, the correct region must be the one common to all three.

That is the central overlap, region D.

options.A: Region A is shared only by saturated triglyceride and haemoglobin. This is incomplete because collagen also has many C=O double bonds in its peptide bonds.
options.B: Region B is shared only by collagen and haemoglobin. This is incomplete because saturated triglyceride also has three C=O double bonds in its three ester bonds.
options.C: Region C is shared only by saturated triglyceride and collagen. This is incomplete because haemoglobin also has many C=O double bonds in its peptide bonds and haem groups.
options.D: Region D is shared by all three molecules. All three have at least two C=O double bonds from their ester bonds or peptide bonds, so D is correct.
